walkthrough:
**Read what point X means**

Look at the graph. Point X is on the steep, rising part of the curve, well before the plateau.

This tells you substrate concentration is still limiting the rate here, because many active sites are still empty and waiting for substrate.

**Check factor 2, substrate concentration**

If you increase substrate concentration at X, there will be more frequent collisions between substrate and enzyme.

More enzyme-substrate complexes form per unit time, so activity increases. Factor 2 is correct.

**Check factors 1 and 3, pH and temperature**

Enzyme activity depends on the precise 3D shape of the active site and on kinetic energy.

A change in pH can alter charges and hydrogen bonds and change the active site shape, while a change in temperature changes kinetic energy and collision rate, and can also denature the enzyme. So both can change activity at X, even when substrate is limiting. Factors 1 and 3 are also correct.

**Put it together**

Since an increase in pH change, substrate concentration, and temperature can all alter the rate at X, all three factors 1, 2 and 3 apply.

That matches option A.

options.A: Correct and reassuring. At X substrate is limiting so more substrate raises rate, and pH and temperature affect active site shape and collision rate, so all three can change activity.
options.B: Close but incomplete. It correctly includes pH and substrate, but wrongly leaves out temperature which also affects kinetic energy and enzyme shape at X.
options.C: Close but incomplete. It correctly includes pH and temperature, but wrongly leaves out substrate concentration which is the limiting factor on the rising part at X.
options.D: Close but incomplete. It correctly includes substrate and temperature, but wrongly leaves out pH which can alter the active site and change activity at X.
